chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-'Inah, and I said, 'Indeed, most of our merchants today give al-'Inah, so let me relate to you how it is done.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go ahead.' I said: 'A haggling man comes to us wanting money, so he haggles with us, and we have no goods. He says, "I will profit you ten, eleven," and I say, "And I, ten, eleven." So we do not cease bargaining until we agree upon a matter.'

When we finish, I say to him, 'Which goods do you prefer that I buy for you?' He says, 'Silk, because we do not find anything less wasteful than it.' So I go, having made a verbal agreement without a formal sale. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if you wish, you do not give it, and if he wishes, he does not take from you?' I said, 'Yes.'

He (the narrator) said: 'So I go and buy that silk for him, and I bargain to the best of my ability. Then I bring it to my house and sell it to him. Sometimes I add a little to him over the verbal agreement, sometimes I give it to him as agreed, and sometimes we struggle and nothing happens. When he buys from me, he does not find anyone more expensive with it than the one from whom I bought it, so he sells it to him. Then he comes, takes the dirhams, and hands them to him; and sometimes he comes to assign it to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You do not hand them over except to the owner of the silk.'

I said: 'And sometimes the sale does not agree between me and him, and I seek from him, and he accepts it from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if he wishes, he does not do it, and if you wish, you do not return it?' I said, 'Yes. If he were to die, it would be from my wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with this. When you do not exceed this, there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الْعِينَة: Buy-back sale (a sale with a repurchase agreement, often used for cash liquidity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on al-'Inah in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the classical 'Inah' mechanism where a merchant sells goods on credit to a cash-needy party, who then immediately resells them for cash to the original seller, effectively creating a loan with interest. Imam al-Rida (AS) validates this practice as permissible (Ja'iz) based on the principle of 'Ikhtiyar' (optionality), noting that since the final sale is not pre-committed and either party can withdraw, it avoids the strict prohibition of Riba in fixed contracts. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the form of the transaction and its substantive economic reality, allowing for liquidity solutions in trade.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq who said, 
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the buy-back (الْعِينَةَ) and I said, ‘The merchants these days are giving the buy-back (الْعِينَةَ)’. 
So I can relate to you how we deal’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give it (explanation)’. I said, ‘The haggling man comes over to us wanting the goods, so we haggle and there are no goods with us. So he is saying, ‘I will profit you ten/eleven (Persian)’, and I am saying, ‘And I, ten/eleven (as well)’. So we do not cease to bargain until we agree upon one bargain.
So when we are free, I say, ‘Which goods are beloved to you that I should buy for you?’ So he is saying, ‘The silk, because we cannot find anything less in wastage than it’. So I go, having given my word without having sold’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it not that if you so desire to, you do not give it, and if he so desires to, he does not take from you?’ I said, ‘Yes’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I go and I buy that silk for him, and I bargain in accordance to my striving. Then I come over with it to my house, and I sell it to him. So, sometimes I increase it (the price) a little bit upon him over the oral contract, and sometimes I give it to him upon what I had orally contracted, and sometimes we get into difficulties, so nothing happens. So when he buys from me, and he does not find anyone more expensive with it than that the one whom I had bought it from, so he sells it to him. So he comes and takes the Dirhams, and he hands it over to him; and sometimes he comes in order to assign it upon me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You cannot hand it over to anyone except the owner of the silk’. 
I said, ‘And sometimes there is no concordance between me and him to sell with, and I seek to him, and he accepts from me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or is it not that if he so desires to he does not do it, and if you so desire to, you do not return it?’ I said, ‘Yes. If he were to dies, so it would be from my wealth’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with this. When you do not exceed this, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Isma’il ibn ‘Abd al-Khaliq who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about ‘Aynah saying, ‘Our merchants in general these days provide ‘Aynah. I like to explain how it is done. He (the Imam) said, ‘Go on and explain.’ I said, ‘A man comes who works in Musaxvamah (fixed price regardless of capital) who wants merchandise on the basis of Musawamah but we do not have any goods and he says, “I give you a profit of dah yazdah” and I say “I give dah dawazdah.” He continues bargaining and we also do so. When we complete I say to him, “Which merchandise you want me to buy for you?” He says, “I like silk because we do not find anything else less depreciating than silk.” I agree and form a contract without selling.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Is it possible that if you did not like you can refuse to give him and if he does not like he does not take from you?’ I replied, ‘Yes, it is possible.

I then go and buy for him that silk and then bargain as much as I can and then I come to my home then sell it to him perhaps with an increase a little more than what is contracted, or perhaps give him for what is contracted, and perhaps we become difficult then nothing happens. ‘Then if he buys from me he cannot find anyone else asking higher price than the one, from whom I bought it, to sell to him. He comes and takes the dirhams and gives it to him or perhaps he comes with an assignment on me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not give it to anyone else beside the owner of silk.’

I then said, ‘Perhaps the sale does not take place between us. I ask him and he agrees.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Is it possible that if he likes, he does not do so and if you want you do not return?’ I replied, ‘Yes, it is possible. If he dies it is from my assets.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is lawful; if you do not violate the condition, then it is not unlawful.’”
